analysis.title: GS EU FINANCIALS SPEC SALES: HSBC, DEPOSITS MIX, POSITIONING, THIS WEEK RESULTS, INSURANCE, FLATEX
key_insights: HSBC missed on top line in 3Q26 and the share price fell about 7%. The desk calls this the first quarter in which bank earnings are being cut, after DNB (the only bank not missing) and Barclays (outperformed on the cost narrative and distribution upside from lower capital requirements).

HSBC time deposits rose from 36% to 38% of deposits QoQ, and the CFO cited a previous peak of 40%. The desk expects consensus to add further mix-shift deterioration, which would lower NII by another 1%.

The desk sees a low single-digit EPS cut for HSBC in 2027, driven by NII and weaker market fees, partly offset by costs. The share price move is read as a de-rating and a communication misstep rather than only an earnings change.

Standard Chartered reports tomorrow. The desk's base case is that it delivers better, because it is less NII-geared and already more weighted to time deposits, which could widen the valuation gap between HSBC and Standard Chartered.

Time deposit share has stayed high in France, Belgium and the Netherlands, so mix shift there should not be material. It fell slightly in Germany, so it can rise again. The open question is behaviour change in low-beta countries such as Ireland and Spain.
Bankinter remains one of the desk's key shorts on the deposit-mix theme because of a structural deposit cost problem between its front book and back book.

Hedge funds de-grossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions and the pace is accelerating. The last such streak was April 2026 and none occurred in 2025. The 22 October de-grossing event was the 5th largest this year and the largest long selling since September 2025.

Long-only funds sold more banks last week, but the size was well below a flow several weeks ago. Hedge fund long/short ratios for banks and insurance are at the lows of recent history. Long-only funds are rotating from banks to insurance while hedge funds are more negative on insurance bottom-up.
Macro, geopolitics and oil prices remain the main driver of further bank sell-offs or recovery. There is also intra-sector rotation into exchanges, with more interest and flow in LSEG.

UK Budget is tomorrow. The base case is an extra 2 to 3pp on the bank tax surcharge, but the desk says the gilt and bond market reaction matters more. Barclays UK printed 7% loan growth with stable NIM and UK GDP data was better.

Desk positioning into this week's results: longs kept in Standard Chartered, Erste, UBS, BCP, NatWest and Piraeus. The desk will be careful on result quality at Santander and NII expectations at ING and Caixa. In France it prefers BNP and SocGen over Credit Agricole.

GS expects the Fed to hold on 28 October and hike 25bp to 4-4.25% on 9 December because spot inflation is too high, with energy-driven upside inflation risk that could prompt another hike in March. Cuts return in late 2027 or early 2028.

GS expects the ECB to hold on 29 October and hike a final time to 2.75% in December. French bond-market turbulence, likely to shave 1/4 to 1/2pp off annualised growth, is a downside risk to that call. GS's strongest global view is that central banks will deliver fewer hikes than priced.

Insurance is not a safe hiding place per the desk. Brown & Brown said CAT property rates in 2027 may be 10 to 20 percent down, with the high end more likely. GS is 1% below company-collected consensus for Allianz 3Q26 operating profit, with P&C and Asset Management each 2% lower.

GS downgraded Gjensidige to Neutral from Buy as pricing normalises and leaves little room to beat high expectations. FY27e-30e EPS is cut by about 2.4% and the 12-month price target is cut 9% to NOK 273.

Flatex: BaFin lowered the group's capital requirement, adding strategic flexibility. GS added EUR 100mn of buybacks in each of the next 3 years and sees the stock at about 9.5x 2027 P/E as deeply discounted. Catalysts are lower consensus on commission per trade, customer growth of about 100k additions in 4Q, and the appointment of a new Supervisory Board Chair.

Hannover Re preview: GS operating profit of EUR 932mn is about 3% above company-collected consensus of EUR 907mn. The combined ratio estimate is 86.1% versus consensus 85.3%, and the new plan comes at the 25 November Investor Day.

M&G preview: GS expects higher rates to cut total AUMA to about GBP 384bn from GBP 387bn at 1H26, but positive net flows, including about GBP 1.7bn of Asset Management net inflows in 3Q26. OTP preview: net income of about HUF 318bn, up 4% QoQ.

Unibail: GS cuts 2026E-2030E EPS by 0 to 2% on higher refinancing costs. Management reiterated 2028 guidance but nearer the lower end, and the 12-month price target is cut to EUR 121.0 from EUR 124.0.

Hatzius expects 2027 global growth to look like 2026, which is in line with potential, but sees downside risks. Energy prices are near or above March and April highs on Middle East escalation fears, and the Fed is effectively ruled out of hiking on 28 October.

GS Risk Appetite Indicator fell to -0.5, the lowest since April 2025, with credit driving the decline. Tech has become a larger driver of cross-asset moves, with the indicator's correlation to Nasdaq 100 relative to S&P 500 equal weight near 1. GS stays modestly pro-risk with overweight equities and underweight credit.

Santander faces EUR 36.85bn of debt maturities in 2027 versus EUR 16.4bn for BBVA, EUR 8.1bn for CaixaBank and EUR 1.9bn for Sabadell, which implies higher financing costs. Consensus for Santander in 2027 is seen as high.

DWS capped withdrawals from its USD 4.8bn Grundbesitz Europa property fund, with investors receiving 10% of requested amounts. Merlin (Buy) benefits from a softened Spanish data-centre decree draft, with the government aiming to approve it before the 29 November election.

Gjensidige downgraded from Buy as pricing normalises and expectations are high. Price target cut 9% and FY27e-30e EPS cut by about 2.4%.
Flatex (FTK) trades at about 9.5x 2027 P/E (GSe) after BaFin cut its Pillar 2 requirement by 100bps. Added buybacks and customer growth are the catalysts.
Unibail 12-month price target cut 2% from EUR 124.0, implying 34% upside, after higher refinancing costs lowered EPS.
Merlin is Buy-rated and GS sees current valuation as pricing overly negative data-centre regulation outcomes.
Desk keeps its long into results. UBS transaction income trends are seen as similar to HSBC's wealth fees.
Bankinter is a key short on the deposit-mix theme because of structural deposit costs in its front book versus back book.

Santander faces EUR 36.85bn of 2027 debt maturities and the desk will be careful on result quality. ING and Caixa NII expectations also get caution.

Not the best hiding place. US CAT property rates are expected down 10 to 20 percent in 2027, Gjensidige pricing is normalising and hedge funds are negative bottom-up.

OW equities for 3m/12m, UW credit for 3m/12m, on earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end.

earnings_insights: HSBC 3Q26 reported underlying PBT US$10.0bn, 4% below GSe and in line with company-compiled consensus. Banking NII was -3% vs GSe and -2% vs consensus, non-banking NII -3% vs GSe and -1% vs consensus.

HSBC 3Q26 credit cost 31bps vs 40bps GSe and 41bps consensus, costs in line. ROTE ex-notables 18.2%, CET1 13.9%, interim dividend US$0.10, buyback up to US$1bn vs GSe US$0.5bn and Visible Alpha range US$0.5-2.5bn.
HSBC net new money (NNM) was US$41bn in 3Q26 with Asia US$38bn, vs 2Q26 NNM US$25bn (Asia US$22bn).
Barclays UK printed 7% loan growth with stable NIM last week. DNB was the only bank not missing numbers this season.

Allianz 3Q26 preview: GS operating profit estimate is about 1% below company-collected consensus (published 26/10/26), with P&C and Asset Management each about 2% lower. Headline COR is about 15bps less favourable than consensus and Solvency II ratio is 1ppt lower.

Hannover Re 3Q26 preview: GS operating profit estimate EUR 932mn vs company-collected consensus EUR 907mn (about 3% above). GS combined ratio estimate 86.1% vs consensus 85.3%. No 2027 net income guidance expected before the 25 November Investor Day.

M&G 3Q26 preview: GS expects about GBP 1.7bn of Asset Management net inflows and AUMA of about GBP 384bn vs GBP 387bn at 1H26. M&G wrote GBP 1.1bn of BPA volumes in July and August vs GBP 0.6bn in 1H26.
OTP 3Q26 preview: GS forecasts net income of about HUF 318bn, up 4% QoQ, with NII up about 2% QoQ and stable group NIM.
Unibail 9M26 review: GS 2026E-2030E EPS cut 0 to 2%, 12-month price target EUR 121.0 (from EUR 124.0).

Flatex: GS added EUR 100mn of annual buybacks in 2027-29 to estimates and values the stock at about 9.5x 2027 P/E (GSe). Management targets about 100k customer additions in 4Q and at least 10% annual growth.
Brown & Brown (BRO) commented that 2027 CAT property rates may fall 10 to 20 percent, and the high end is more likely.
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report this week, and the Nasdaq 100 and other equity markets price larger moves this week.

risk_factors: Further deposit mix shift toward time deposits in low-beta countries such as Ireland and Spain, which would lower NII beyond current consensus.
Oil price and Middle East escalation affecting the economy and driving further bank sell-offs.
Continued hedge fund de-grossing and long selling in global equities.
UK Budget bank tax surcharge increase and a weak gilt market reaction.
French bond-market turbulence tightening financial conditions and weighing on ECB policy flexibility.
US mid-term elections and AI-driven tech sell-off, with Tech now a dominant driver of cross-asset risk appetite.
Softening property and casualty pricing for insurers, with reserve and claims inflation uncertainty.
Higher refinancing costs for real estate (Unibail) and higher 2027 debt maturities for Santander.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds de-grossed global equities in 7 of the past 8 sessions with the pace accelerating. The last such streak was April 2026 and none occurred in 2025.
22 October was the 5th largest de-grossing event this year at -1.6 SD, driven entirely by long selling and the largest long selling since September 2025.
Long-only funds sold more banks last week, but the flow was smaller than a few weeks ago. Hedge fund L/S ratios for banks and insurance are at lows versus recent history.
Long-only funds are rotating from banks to insurance while hedge funds are more negative on insurance bottom-up. There is also rotation into exchanges, with more interest and flow in LSEG.

Options markets price more uncertainty over the next 2 weeks than the following month. Nasdaq 100 and other equity indices price larger moves this week (Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings), while long-dated USTs and HY credit price larger moves next week around the US mid-terms.
GS Risk Appetite Indicator at -0.5, the lowest since April 2025. Readings below -1 and especially near -2 have been useful contrarian signals.
geopolitical: War in Iran and fears of renewed Middle East escalation, pushing gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and European and Asian natural gas near or above March and April highs.
Lingering drag from higher US tariffs on global growth.
French bond-market turbulence and OAT-Bund spread widening.
US mid-term elections next week, with long-dated Treasuries and HY credit pricing larger moves around them.
UK Budget on 28 October and potential increase in the bank tax surcharge.
Spanish general election on 29 November and the data-centre Royal Decree.
Brazilian elections cited as context for Santander headlines.

tension_points.bull_case: Time deposit share stays high in France, Belgium and the Netherlands so mix shift there is small. Standard Chartered is less NII-geared and already more weighted to time deposits, so it may deliver better than HSBC.
tension_points.bear_case: HSBC's time deposits rose from 36% to 38% with a prior peak of 40%, and consensus may cut NII by another 1%. Low-beta countries such as Ireland and Spain are a question mark, and Germany's time deposit share fell slightly and could rise again.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Standard Chartered delivering worse than expected on NII or deposits tomorrow would undercut the view that HSBC is the outlier.

tension_points.bull_case: UK loan growth is strong, GDP data was better, and Barclays UK printed 7% loan growth with stable NIM.
tension_points.bear_case: The Budget could raise the bank tax surcharge by an extra 2 to 3pp, and a weak gilt reaction would hurt appetite to reinvest in the UK.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A poor bond and gilt market reaction to tomorrow's Budget would undermine the more optimistic UK read.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations to help equities into year-end, and the Risk Appetite Indicator is not yet negative enough to be a contrarian sell signal.
tension_points.bear_case: AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility. Credit has sold off and hedge funds are de-grossing at an accelerating pace.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Risk Appetite Indicator reading near -2 would flip to a contrarian buy signal, per GS's historical use of the indicator.
